Question: «Accustom him to them» sister Nawaal finds difficult. How do you accustom the children in an attractive manner to the salaah? How do you do that with a teenager?
Answer: In principle you have for that more than 12 or 13 years. The first years from 0 to 6 you stimulate him, make the salaah beloved to him. And you yourself perform it at least five times. The child will undoubtedly — except if Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa wants something else with him — undoubtedly get used to it because he sees that daily. Then it has become for him his life. Apart from that he must be commanded to it from 7 years, every day every salaah. Every salaah he is stimulated, this is accustoming, until 10 years. And that applies also to the rest of the deeds. When the child sees a certain deed with the father/mother, then he gets used to it. And therefore it is important that you begin the upbringing as early as possible, from the year zero. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa says: «وأمُر أَهلَكَ بالصلاةِ واصطَبِر عليها، لا نَسأَلُكَ رِزقًا، نحن نَرزُقُكَ، والعاقبةُ للتَّقوى» (سورة طه: ١٣٢). Interpretation of the meaning: «And command your family the salaah and persevere in it. We ask you no provision, We provide you, and the [good] end is for the piety» (Soerat Taa Haa, verse 132). That is also a form of upbringing of the soul by praying yourself and being patient in the salaah and being patient in stimulating the command to the salaah. In the end you get used to that too by the practicing of the thinking scheme.
Question: How is it with the non-Muslim female friends and friends with your children?
Answer: They must be turned away from. You begin the turning away by letting the child find the shirk and the bad behavior disgusting. That continues until you also make clear to him that he may not deal with the bad people, and the bad people are the people who do not pray, who do not wear the hidjaab, and likewise the disbelievers. On the one hand we must deal with them in a good manner and on the other hand not have a close friendship with them. This is a building from the beginning, we will speak about it, in shaa-a Allaah, later at the social upbringing.
Question: What if the child comes home and says that he/she wants to play at a female friend's [place]? How do you deal with that, because you do not know how the parents are?
Answer: If they are Muslims, then we go to get to know them and their upbringing. And if they are not Muslims, then we also do not have to get to know them and we must turn [the child] away from them by in any case turning [him] away from dealing with them. That begins already at the choosing of the school. You must not choose a school in which there are disbelievers, in which it is normal for a child to play with the children of the disbelievers, and be nice to them as if there is no objection at all. Of course the children are innocent, but they are raised by their parents with the upbringing of their parents. The matter is first about their parents, are they Muslims and are they not Muslims. Not Muslims, then it is finished, and the Muslims if they pray and raise the children in the correct manner, and the mother wears the hidjaab. One must look at this.
So if she has gotten to know her mother and her father and it was a righteous family and a righteous household, then there is no objection, but if that was not good, then [the child] must be kept away and must be made clear why [he] was kept away. Make clear to her that she must look more at others who please Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa and worship Allaah and wear the hidjaab. That is possible, and that is easy.
Ensure that these children are advised to go and pray. That they get their chance when they play at school so they advise them to turn towards the salaah, to turn towards the mosque, and so on.
Follow-up question: You just spoke about children who are friends of disbelieving children. If you as a parent place your child in a non-Islamic primary school — for example because there is no Islamic school in the neighborhood — may that be seen as a sin?
Answer: This is a sin and it can be a major sin, because you in reality destroy your child.
Question: How do you deal with it if your child says something during an open situation that you would rather not have, for example: that girl put on lipstick and received many compliments. How must you respond to that? And at interest in make-up? May you stimulate that to be done only at home, or do you keep [it] away?
Answer: The child must in reality from the child age be stimulated and raised on the system of the reward and the punishment of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. And that means that the child from a young age has only one scale, namely the scale of the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. Then you can talk with him with: does Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa love this or not? Will Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa be happy with this or not? And if he nevertheless keeps insisting, then we have the parental authority that must be exercised at that moment. The question that you must thus pose to the child is: will Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa love you through this or not?
Is the scale that the people like this, or is the scale that Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa likes that or approves it?
That is the question that you must keep in mind and repeat several times until the scale enters the head and becomes a kind of thinking scale, the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
If the child does not grow up on this, then it will be difficult for the child.
Today the shaykh experienced with a child in Daar al-Hudaa that his parents called him and said: we will buy a ticket for a football match for you at 14:00, while he must be in the lesson. They would not have done that at a regular school, but at «Ivoe», at the Qur'aan school or the weekend school, they do that. This can mean several matters:
Either that the child is not in their hand, so they give him what he wants and think thereby that they stimulate him and/or do not lose him thereby.
Or something else, namely that they themselves give a bad example and do not give these lessons the value that they have.
Often it is the one or the other, but sometimes it is a mixture of both. When it is a mixture of both, then the matter is even worse.
One must be very vigilant in this and draw up programs for that so that this becomes the manner of thinking and the manner of communication, the only one between the parent and the child: the pleasure of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa.
The use of make-up before the marriage, and going out with it, may not be stimulated, not even the trying out of it, because you open with it for the child a door to lightheartedness. The child must be kept away from that until she approaches the marriage: she is betrothed, she is going to marry, then she begins to try out these matters for her house, for her husband. Before that she may not do that.
Question: Someone who does not have a good circle of friends: he does not call them friends and finds it difficult to take distance. How can you advise someone to take distance from a wrong company?
Answer: You must first let him find what these friends do disgusting out of sincerity for Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. When you deal with the foundation, then the branch will be easier, but when you do not deal with the foundation and the child had no sincerity in it, then the branch will be difficult. But if you deal with it from the foundation by letting him find these bad deeds disgusting and being sincere to Allaah, and that has not reached him, then you use the authority and the compulsion towards the good.
So before you advise him to leave the friends, you advise him to leave what the friends do.
Question: The matter is about the games, the activities (the offering of useful possibilities for fun). Are little balls in which there are other little balls allowed? When is it a musical instrument? When does a sound belong to just a sound and when to music?
Answer: Little balls in other little balls, that is allowed.
When is it music? It is music when actually a musical instrument is used and music is made.
The sister: [There are] many games that make a kind of melodies, is that also music?
The shaykh: Yes, the melody is music.
Question: From which age must you teach your child to recognize this?
Answer: From the age of 0 years. We spoke about this much, and we will speak about that later in a clearer manner, in shaa-a Allaah, when we speak about the drawing up of a program.
Question: A nephew plays in different manners: sometimes he finishes everything and sometimes not. How do you know what indicates his personality?
Answer: That can be connected with different causes. It can be that his not finishing something [is] that he does not care much about it, or at that moment that he does not finish [it] something else interests him more than what he is occupied with. Thereby you also know what distracts him from others and where his desire inclines and what he loves most. Or it can be that he is quickly distracted, and that he is not a person who does not finish things. Then you must stimulate him in another manner. You stimulate him to finish matters and to be patient in that. So it can thus be connected with different aspects, and you must get to know the child much more to know what it is connected with.
Question: How must I admonish the children of others if the child is not known to the sister and the child did not behave with etiquette and seeks the limits?
Answer: A general admonishing. And if the child accepts the authority, then you exercise the authority too.
Question: Must you respond immediately if you notice and see that the child responds in a bad manner?
Answer: He responds in a bad manner, then you must first point him to the manner in which Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa loves that he responds and whether he has at that moment the right to be angry or not to be angry, and whether Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa loves that or not, and then only you move on to the next.
Follow-up question: May that immediately? If you are — for example — in the company of others?
Answer: If she did that openly, try then to take her aside and advise her. And if she refuses, then you must do that also openly. And if — after you had wanted to advise her openly — she goes to misbehave openly after you had tried to cover her, then you must rebuke her and admonish her openly.
The sister: And if it is at home, then you must first point her to the manner: does Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa love the manner in which she responds?
The shaykh: Yes.
Question: May the children play alone or with other children together upstairs, because you do not know then what they do if you are not with them and what they say?
Answer: The advice is that [there] is an older child or a parent and that you never leave them alone.
Question: [There is] a program «Home Alone» in which they leave the children alone at home, an experiment. What is your opinion about it?
Answer: The shaykh does not know the program. But leaving the children alone at home is done only by parents who in the end want to find their children in «Veilig Thuis» [Safe at Home, the child protection service]. That is unwise and not correct and can lead to danger. It is a matter that is in reality not allowed because it brings very many dangers, and especially when the children are small, young of age. But if the children are [the age of] 10 and 11 and 12 years and are somewhat aware in the sense that they are calm and do not do strange things, [and] know what the dangers are and do not touch them. In case of necessity the shaykh does that, but then you keep a phone with them so that you have continuous contact, but that only in case of necessity. The program itself the shaykh does not know.
Question: From which age must you separate the girls and the boys?
Answer: From when they can distinguish between the two genders. In reality you must from the child age already stimulate the child according to his gender. If it is a girl from two/three years to stimulate her according to her gender. And the boy too. Concerning the clothing, the play, the people. That does not mean that you must forbid, but you stimulate and keep away. From 7 years you must try to separate them. If they are aware early, then you must also separate them early. It is not an Islamic obligation to separate them early.
Question: A number of games were mentioned with which one may not play. Are board games allowed? The sisters find it difficult [to determine] what is and is not allowed. Because dice games are not allowed.
Answer: Card games concerning memory games (memory), that is allowed. Card games such as dolls that move from one place to another — like a kind of monopoly — if they use a die, then they are not allowed because it is a form of gambling. Gambling is not allowed. Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa and the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam have forbidden it. Gambling is not allowed. Playing cards (cards, card games with men and women and hearts and the like) are not allowed because it is a form of gambling (a game that is connected with gambling). As long as something is a gambling game, it is not allowed. You have nowadays also card games that are not gambling and with which you can go from one side to the other without a die.
Those are questions and answers and a point system. That is allowed and there is no objection to it. Everything that has connection with gambling is not allowed.
Follow-up question: Are draughts [draughts] and chess allowed?
Answer: Draughts is allowed as long as it does not distract from the acts of worship and wastes the time, then it is allowed. Chess too, as long as it does not distract from the obligations. Sometimes a chess match lasts weeks and sometimes months. Then they leave the chess match as it is and think and then resume [it]. Then you are occupied more than necessary.
Follow-up question: Are Islam quizzes and prizes allowed?
Islam quizzes are allowed and the prizes are allowed as long as there is not paid. As long as there is not paid, it is allowed.
Question: In the document about the upbringing of the 3aqiedah there was a number of matters to stimulate the child to say «Allaahu akbar, Subhaana-llaah», and so on. She did that continuously with her nephew and her niece. She noticed then that their attention was not always focused on that. She found it difficult to get their attention while she wanted to teach it to them.
The shaykh: How old are they?
The sister: The niece [is] about a year [old], and the nephew [is] about two years [old], and his pronunciation is reasonably good, maa shaa-a Allaah. What she did in the past weeks is the continuous repeating, and Subhaana-llaah he pronounces the words now, and she is happy with that. She adopted the methodology of repeating, but she does not know whether that is the correct methodology that you advise, but she sees that it has an effect.
The shaykh: The repeating is good, but in a stimulating manner, in a manner in which the child likes to repeat it. But not only repeating but also performing it yourself in the presence of the child in a spontaneous manner in which the child sees it as something that he too must do. Whether the attention of the child is present or not, as long as they hear and keep hearing, several times, then they will repeat that. It is not a lesson in which they are completely focused. They are children, they pick [it] up without looking at you, without showing that they are focused. They simply pick up the matters.
The sister: On the advice of sisters she made a song form in the form of a little song, and that really had an effect, [and] she keeps singing that song. Is it allowed to teach the children the words of the dhikr in the form of singing?
Answer: [There is] a difference between the singing and the poetry. The singing in which one goes to dance a half dance is not correct. But the poetry form in which there is a rhyme and that sounds more beautiful than the ordinary speech, is allowed.
The sister: So she applied the poetry form.
Question: The Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam sought refuge [for] al-Hasan and al-Husayn and said: «أُعيذُكما بكَلِماتِ الله التامَّةِ من كلِّ شيطانٍ وهامَّةٍ، ومن كلِّ عَينٍ لامَّة». Interpretation of the meaning: «I seek refuge for you both with the perfect words of Allaah against every shaytaan and [every] poisonous vermin, and against every evil [envious] eye». When can you supplicate with this narrated supplication for your child? When/at which moment did the Prophet sallallaahu 3alayhi wa sallam perform this supplication for his two grandsons?
Answer: This supplication you can mention from the year 0, from the first day.
The sister: Do you use the supplication extra at special moments?
The shaykh: [There is] no special moment for that, but for example when other people see him, before others see him so that they do not strike him with the [evil] eye, when he wakes up, when he sleeps.
Question: A question about the Names of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa. Do you have advice [about] where we can read about the Names of Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa? And how can one, regarding the explanation, give the Names of Allaah to the children in the best manner?
Answer: [There is] a beautiful book by shaykh 3Abdu-Rrazzaaq al-Badr, and it is translated. The translation the shaykh does not know, but he leafed through it a bit. It seemed acceptable. The original content of that book is a beautiful content. Often the English is translated better. «The Beautiful Names» by imaam Ibn al-Qayyim, if it is translated, then it is also good.
Those are the books that are translated as far as the shaykh knows.
Question: 9 steps were discussed for the realizing of the upbringing of the 3aqiedah. The sisters read them with each other before the lesson about the upbringing of the 3aqiedah. We had then a question whether you can explain each point more with many examples, but according to what I believe you have already done that. What is wise in this now?
Answer: As far as the shaykh knows we did that last time. But what we will do: we now mention different kinds of upbringing per age with explanation how you must do that. Then we will speak about how you can draw up a weekly and daily program for a child. Then we will also speak about how you use the various means in that. Then we will also speak about how you can apply that practically with the many obstacles, and the temptations, and the challenges that the parents encounter. And among what we will discuss is the bad behavior, how you can improve the bad behavior, repair it, remove it. And how you can connect the origin of the bad behavior and the bad behavior itself. All these matters we will clarify, in shaa-a Allaah. We live in a very dangerous situation for the parents and the children together.
You must create a kind of immunity in yourself and also in the child. That he will still explain, in shaa-a Allaah. The shaykh does not want us to enter into subject-matter details of some aspects, some topics. Why do we not enter into the details of it subject-wise? Because that would then become a lesson of Islamic studies, then we fall behind a year and a half.
Question: How is the position of the mother preserved while the mistake is corrected?
May the man correct his wife (the mother of the children) in the presence of the children?
Answer: The man must in principle not correct his wife in the presence of the children, but when it has an influence on the children and the wife/mother keeps repeating this matter in the presence of the children, then the man must correct the woman partially in the presence of the children, whereby the mother corrects herself in the presence of the children and acknowledges her mistake in the presence of the children. That also makes her [more] a mother. Your children will revere you more because they know that you, despite that you are a mother, also make mistakes and correct your mistake too. Many parents let their children think: «We are without mistakes and you may not make mistakes». Then that gap becomes very big between the one who has no mistake and the one who makes mistakes every day. The parents are not without mistakes, but they do not correct themselves in the presence of the children when they make the mistake in the presence of the children. They do influence their children but do not correct themselves in the presence of the children. That is a big mistake. That ensures that the children no longer make an effort to correct themselves, because the good in their eyes is that you cover the mistakes with a shine and are without mistakes. And that is a bad example.
So if the mother makes a mistake in the presence of her children and that mistake has an influence on the children, then her husband must not correct her in the presence of the children at first glance. But if the matter repeats and the wife becomes stubborn and then goes to make this mistake intentionally in the presence of the children, then the man must correct the wife in the presence of the children. But if the man notices that his wife, when he speaks to her aside, will go to correct herself, but then she must correct herself afterwards at the children by saying: I made a mistake, this mistake may not be repeated, and you may not imitate me in this mistake because Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa does not love this. So she must correct herself in the presence of the children, and the man corrects her aside. As long as that goes well, that simply continues. But at the moment that that does not go well and the woman goes to misbehave intentionally in the presence of the children and also goes to say something about it, because some women are so arrogant that they say: «No, I want the children to hear this, the children may not receive your upbringing», then it is important that the woman is calmed at that moment and that it is also made clear to the children by papa that mama at that moment made a mistake despite that she does not want to correct herself. That is at further escalation. The woman, the mother, must correct herself at the children.
Question: May I as a woman advise my husband in the presence of the children with preservation of the position of the father?
Answer: If the advice means that he is advised about a sin, then no, or about a mistake that he made with the children, then no. Then that too must be performed aside, and he must correct himself if he has done that in the presence of the children, so he must talk with the children who saw that: «I made such and such a mistake, may Allaah subhaanahu wa ta3aalaa forgive me, you may not make this mistake».
Question: That is about the children who have not reached the buloegh yet. Are the children forgiven until their buloegh, and do the children under 7 years receive a bad point?
Answer: It is not [so] that they are forgiven. Their sins are not written until the buloegh. But they receive a black point on their hearts or a white point, so their hearts are indeed influenced. Everything that the human being sees and hears and feels influences the heart. But concerning the writing of the bad deeds, no, until the buloegh.
